skill.name: webask-source-dashboard
skill.description: Сравнивает, откуда приходят респонденты опроса WebAsk и какие каналы дают лучший результат. Применяется, когда человек спрашивает, какая рассылка или реклама сработала, или хочет разложить ответы по источникам.
skill.summary: Compare WebAsk survey sources by response count, completion rate, and a selected outcome using existing source tags.
skill.author: webaskio

content.value_statement: Survey totals can hide differences between recruitment channels. This skill guides your assistant to compare tagged WebAsk responses by volume, completion rate, and your selected outcome.
actual_capabilities: Check available source tag values with get_answer_extra_field_values before comparing channels.
Request filtered survey reports for each source tag through get_quiz_report.
Present a channel table with response counts, completion rates, and a selected outcome such as contact count or average rating.
Sort channels by the metric that matters to the user.
Keep untagged responses in a separate row and warn about small sample sizes.
Summarize response volume, completion performance, and weaker outcomes in the language used by the user.
limitations: Source attribution requires tags already present in responses; missing tags cannot be recovered retrospectively.
Requires access to the external WebAsk MCP tools; their implementations are not included in this skill.
Small samples and a single survey run do not establish reliable channel rankings or justify stopping a channel.
Produces an assistant report, not a standalone dashboard application, and stops when service limits prevent further reporting.

use_cases.title: Compare campaign channels
use_cases.description: Compare tagged email, messaging, and website responses by completion rate and collected contact count.

use_cases.title: Assess survey recruitment
use_cases.description: Review response volume and completion across recruitment sources while keeping small samples and untagged responses visible.

use_cases.title: Review feedback by source
use_cases.description: Compare average ratings across tagged invitation channels and identify differences that need further investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Check source tags
prompt_templates.prompt: Check which source tags exist for WebAsk survey [survey]. Tell me whether a channel comparison is possible.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: verify that attribution data exists.

prompt_templates.title: Compare channel completion
prompt_templates.prompt: For WebAsk survey [survey], compare sources by response count and completion rate. Sort by completion rate and show untagged responses separately.

prompt_templates.title: Rank by a selected outcome
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare sources for WebAsk survey [survey] using [outcome] as the primary metric. Include response counts, completion rates, and small-sample warnings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: focus the report on a business outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate channel tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze WebAsk survey [survey] by source, prioritizing [outcome]. Contrast volume, completion, and outcome quality; separate untagged responses and explain uncertainty. Do not recommend stopping channels based on this run alone.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: interpret differences without overstating the evidence.

output_examples.input: Using the illustrative campaign data, compare sources by collected contacts.
output: Illustrative results, sorted by collected contacts:
Website banner: 68 responses, 15 completed, 22% completion, 9 contacts.
Email leads in response volume, completion rate, and collected contacts.
The banner has the lowest completion rate; investigate message alignment before drawing conclusions about the channel.
One run does not justify stopping a channel.

output_examples.input: Compare channels for a survey with no source tags.
output: No source tags were found, so a channel comparison is unavailable.
Existing responses cannot be attributed retrospectively from arrival times.
Add source tags to distribution links before the next survey run.

best_practices: Use consistent source tags on distribution links before collecting responses.
Select the outcome metric before ranking channels, and review it alongside response counts and completion rates.
Keep untagged responses visible and qualify comparisons involving small samples.
anti_patterns: Guessing missing source attribution from response arrival times.
Treating response volume alone as proof of channel quality.
Stopping a channel based on one survey run or a small sample.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Your environment must provide access to the required WebAsk MCP tools.

faq.question: What data does it need?
faq.answer: It needs a WebAsk survey with existing source tags and access to tag values and filtered survey reports.

faq.question: Can it identify sources when tags are missing?
faq.answer: No. It keeps untagged responses separate and does not infer their sources from response timing.

faq.question: Does it modify survey responses?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses two read-only reporting tools. It does not instruct the assistant to modify survey responses.

faq.question: Does it create a dashboard application?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to produce a channel comparison table and three conclusions, not a standalone application.

faq.question: What happens when a WebAsk limit is reached?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to explain the limit and stop, without recommending a plan change or directing you to payment.
